We were with two Warrior on this occasion, again in my 432 ambulance, and the convoy was commanded by Captain Jack Ferguson, one staffer's officer who was attached to the battle group, and he had severe difficulties in negotiating our way through the HVO checkpoint because there was a battle -- a firefight going on between the two sides of what had been once a mixed village with the BiH and the HVO fighting and we -- they wanted to use us as a shield, I guess, in order to try and reduce the fighting. We took the -- he took the decision on the ground that we would go tactical. In other words, we would turn our lights off and drive at full speed through the checkpoint and beyond, and in the process of that, build-up to that, they -- we had been surrounded by HVO fighters whom -- with RPG 7s which would, once again, have caused me greater difficulty than it would have done the two Warrior because, as I previously mentioned, they are armoured with protective chobham sides which I didn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could you explain, what is an RPG 7?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: A rocket-propelled grenade. It's a hand-held weapons system.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So eventually you managed --

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: We drove, as I said, tactically, as fast as we could with our convoy lights on, which are just lights really underneath the vehicles so you can't actually see the vehicles so well. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Were you shot at when you were actually driving away?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: The vehicle noise was so intense because of you accelerating so hard, I don't recollect whether we were or whether we weren't. Certainly there were no rounds came -- certainly no rounds came through the 432 on that -- through my vehicle on that occasion, and we only put our lights back on and slowed down once we were back on the main Bugojno-Gornji Vakuf road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Two more topics. One is do you know whether Muslim civilians were ever forcibly removed from their villages by the HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: The -- I never witnessed Muslim personnel being forcibly removed. I had stories told to me by villagers that that had happened. For example, in -- in Dusa, the -- the men had been forcibly removed in their trucks. And I also had cause to remember one other particular incident when I had cause again to do some psychological support for one of the infanteers who had been on the ground and had been witness to two individuals who had been killed in the village where also the villagers had been forced -- forced to leave, but it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that village?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 01373, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: We -- we've seen this report before.

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And I'd like you to move down to -- to the bottom of the first page. If the document could be scrolled down, please. And could you please read out the last sentence of this last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: "The local BiH command were reported to be demanding compensation in cash for all the Muslim families who have been forced to move as a result of ethnic cleansing."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did -- did you ever hear about this, that the BiH command was demanding compensation for -- for Muslim families?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: I never heard about it from the families on the ground, although I was aware of it from meetings that happened at the base, the kind of meetings we've referred to earlier with BiH and HVO local commanders, and it was a topic that I do recall being discussed at -- at at least one of those meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, just one last matter. Did you ever -- were you ever involved in exchange of bodies, and do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: Yeah. As I previously mentioned, one of my meetings with Colonel Siljeg, the issue of body exchanges was on the agenda of that meeting. My recollection is that was towards the end of January, 1993. And the arrangements were initially tabled, and then, because that was predominantly ICRC business, was very much organised by ICRC with the involvement of B Company 1 Cheshire's Battle Group being to supervise the actual crossover of HVO and BiH dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And how did you get involved in this exchange?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: I was -- I was -- I sat in on some of the planning meetings. There was no requirement for medical involvement because we were dealing with the exchange of dead bodies and not of living people, not prisoners of war or anything of the sort. However, my involvement became a little bit more than anticipated because when the body exchange actually did happen, the call-sign on the ground, Colour Williams -- Colour Sergeant Williams, to whom we referred to the intelligence cell senior NCO, who was a trained medic, discovered that one of the BiH fighters who had been placed at the bottom of the pile in the truck was in fact alive, and so he got on the radio to me in order to ask for medical advice as to how to manage the individual. And then I also had cause to do some psychological support, debriefing, whatever you'd like to call it, with him after the event because of some of the things that he'd seen, and he needed to talk through that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So you were on the phone, but do you know where this exchange actually took place?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: I know it took place within Gornji Vakuf opstina. It clearly wasn't right by the -- let's say the centre of town. It wasn't by the crossroads, because that would have made sense for me to go down to see the casualty myself. It would have been -- it would have made more sense for me to go to carry out the treatment there. But it certainly wasn't an hour or more away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 01308. And, Your Honours, I'm almost done, so I don't know if you want me to continue tomorrow morning or whether I can finish the testimony, which will take five more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, finish within the five minutes then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So if the witness could be shown Exhibit 1308, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: Can I ask you -- can I ask them to scroll it down? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, could you read out the text that is -- that is on this document. ?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: "The captured Muslims are to collect --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, ma'am. Mr. Siljeg -- Is she aware of this document? If he can lay a foundation, fine; if not, we ought to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only reason I'm showing this document is whether she can recognise whether this was the exchange that she has just given testimony about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: She can just look at the date or something but she's being asked to read this aloud into the record, a document which she doesn't know. He can lay the foundation. If he cannot lay the foundation, then he might go some other route.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, Witness, could you read this document to yourself and tell me whether what is in the document is in fact the same exchange that you have been talking about, and why you think it would be the same exchange.

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: I have read -- read the document, and I would be happy to state that I believe that to be the same exchange to which I referred earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And for what reason?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: The arrangements were that the dead would be collected by their captured of their own side. The exchange was -- was related to the heavy fighting that had gone on in the Partisan cemetery in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And as far as the date is concerned?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: And the date would fit in exactly with that, that to which I referred earlier, and the signature being Colonel Siljeg relates therefore back to the meeting where this was originally discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Two more questions. Did there come a time in February where the conflict actually calmed down and -- as the result of a cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: The fighting did calm down actually at a time whilst I was away from Gornji Vakuf on my two weeks' break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And how would you describe the situation in that period that followed the cease-fire in the last two months of your duty?

utterances.speaker: JACQUELINE CARTER
utterances.text: It was a very tense and brittle environment in which we were now working. There was an awful lot of hatred and mistrust. The villages where four months previously had been mixed were now very much divided with -- if they were still inhabited by both sides with central areas that were completely no-go-zone areas for both sides. And there was a feeling that -- reports from people on the ground, and the feeling as you lived amongst it, that business was not finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: That closes my examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bos. So the examination-in-chief has been completed. Madam, you'll be back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in order to answer questions put to you by the Defence counsel within the frameworks of the cross-examination. Between now and then, please don't make contact with either the representatives of the OTP or the Defence counsel, and of course not the Judges either. So having said that, we reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00, and please be here on time. 9.00 sharp. Thank you.
